prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2019 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: Tackle the climate and ecological emergency while delivering social justice, democratic renewal and shared prosperity. The flagship Green New Deal invests £100+ billion per year (plus UBI) to reach net zero carbon by 2030, create millions of green jobs and improve quality of life.

Green New Deal priorities
- Energy: Rapid expansion of wind (around 70% of electricity by 2030), plus solar, tidal, hydro and geothermal; double grid capacity, boost storage and demand management; end fossil subsidies, introduce a rising Carbon Tax, ban fracking, prohibit new nuclear, expand interconnectors.
- Housing: Insulate every home by 2030; deep retrofit 1 million homes/year; 1 million rooftop renewables by 2030; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard social homes/year; heat pumps and heat networks; raise rental energy standards to EPC A.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify key routes; reopen stations and local lines; bring rail into public ownership; expand buses/trams with local control; £2.5bn/yr for walking and cycling; cancel HS2 and new road capacity; stop new runways; frequent flyer levy; end sale of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030; 20mph default in residential areas.
- Industry: Clean-tech standards, grants to replace high-carbon kit, circular economy, right to repair (10-year warranties), reduce F-gases, CCS for steel/cement, £2bn/yr for skills and apprenticeships, regional mutual banks.
- Food, farming & forestry: 10-year shift to agroecology; refocus subsidies; cut pesticides by 50% by weight by 2022; 700 million trees; rewilding; right to food; clearer labelling; phased tax on meat/dairy with revenues recycled to farmers; flood prevention via nature-based solutions.

Secure incomes and homes
- Universal Basic Income: Adults £89/week; pensioners £178/week; supplements for disabled, carers, lone parents and children; retain Housing Benefit; no one worse off.
- Work and living: Living Wage £12 (incl. 16–21-year-olds); 10:1 pay ratio cap; gig worker rights; 35 hours/week free childcare from 9 months; progress toward shorter working week.
- Renters: Rent controls tied to local incomes, end no-fault evictions, support co-ops and community-led housing.

Democracy and government reform
- Proportional representation for all elections; votes at 16; elected second chamber; party funding reform; Digital Bill of Rights; citizens’ assemblies; devolve powers and +£10bn/yr to councils, £3bn/yr climate adaptation fund; free home care at home for over-65s.
- Create a Carbon Chancellor with a yearly Carbon Budget; Future Generations Act; replace Home Office with Ministries for Sanctuary and Interior; pivot defence to Security and Peace; end arms export promotion.

Public services and nature
- NHS: +£6bn/yr (rising to 2030), end internal market, expand community/mental/reproductive health, reinstate nursing bursaries.
- Education: +£4bn/yr; smaller classes; start formal schooling at 6; scrap Ofsted/league tables; free university (scrap tuition fees, write off £9k-era debt); boost FE/adult education; climate and nature curriculum.
- Nature: Ecocide law; stronger planning protections; right to roam in England/Wales; 30% of UK waters fully protected by 2030; ban harmful pesticides, peat burning; urban greening.

Rights, justice and drugs
- End hostile environment; humane immigration with right to work; tackle misogyny as hate crime; strengthen LGBTIQA+ and disability rights.
- Halve prison population via prevention/restorative justice; invest in youth services.
- End the war on drugs: legalise/regulate with health-led approach; prescription heroin; legal cannabis; tax revenues fund services.

Animals
- Recognise animal sentience; ban hunting, live exports, factory-farming cruelties; end badger cull; curb animal testing; new Animal Protection Commission.

Funding and tax
- Operational spend: ~£141.5bn/yr funded by Carbon Tax (~£76.7bn), consolidated income tax (merging NI/CGT/Dividends/Inheritance/Income), higher corporation tax (24%), bank taxes, anti-avoidance, sin taxes.
- Capital: Borrow ~£94.4bn/yr for grid, renewables, housing retrofit/build, rail, EV infrastructure; catalyse ~£50bn/yr private investment.
- Reform land and property tax: Replace Council Tax/Business Rates with Land Value Tax over 10 years, shifting burden to landowners, with protections.
- Cancel wasteful projects: Trident, major new roads, HS2, airport expansion, Help to Buy; end NHS internal market.
- Europe: Campaign to Remain via a People’s Vote; democratise and green the EU; uphold freedom of movement; humane refugee policy; EU carbon border measures.
- International: Aid to 1% of GNI focused on climate/poverty; ethical trade (no ISDS); ecocide law; protect indigenous rights.
